No separate issue since it's a one-line comment fix.

body.title: Session responses carry nothing that keeps a shared cache from storing them
body.body:
Right now when a handler reads a session and answers with something that depends on it, the response goes out without any caching directive. The docs do mention CDNs in the idle timeout note, saying that a response with `Set-Cookie` is usually not stored and that requests that only read the session set no cookie at all, but that second case is exactly the one where nothing stops a cache keyed by URL from keeping one user's response and serving it to the next one.

I went through what other frameworks do here and most of them don't leave it to the app:

- Django's [session middleware](https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py) adds `Vary: Cookie` whenever the session was accessed, modified or not.
- Symfony's [session listener](https://github.com/symfony/symfony/blob/7.4/src/Symfony/Component/HttpKernel/EventListener/AbstractSessionListener.php) makes the response private as soon as the session is started, with a header to opt out, and its responses default to `no-cache, private` anyway, which Laravel inherits.
- Rails [defaults every response](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/main/actionpack/lib/action_dispatch/http/cache.rb) to `max-age=0, private, must-revalidate`.
- PHP's default [session cache limiter](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.session-cache-limiter.php) is `nocache`, which sends `no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate`.
- Spring Security [adds](https://docs.spring.io/spring-security/reference/features/exploits/headers.html) `no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate` by default and backs off when the app sets its own.
- express-session does nothing, same as h3 today.

We could either do:

1. Add a warning in the session docs next to that note, telling people that a response built from session data should be sent as private and not storable.
2. Appending `Vary: Cookie` when a session is read from the cookie, like Django does, or going the Symfony way and marking the response private with a way to opt out.

I can send a PR for either of them, I just wanted to check first which direction you'd prefer.

body.title: fix(response): merge `Vary` instead of overwriting it when merging prepared headers
body.body:
Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code, on behalf of Magnus

Fixes #1642

When a handler returns a `Response` (or throws an `HTTPError` with its own headers), h3 merges the headers staged on `event.res.headers` / `event.res.errHeaders` into it. Every header except `set-cookie` was merged with `set`, so a `Vary` staged by middleware replaced the response's own `Vary`. With the example from the issue, `Vary: Cookie` from the handler was lost and only `Accept-Encoding` was sent, which lets a shared cache hand one user's response to another.

Now, when both sides have a `Vary`, the staged entries are added to the response's own list, skipping names it already has (compared case-insensitively). If only one side has a `Vary`, nothing changes. The same merge is used for error headers, so `errHeaders` and `HTTPError.headers` are combined the same way.

Tests: two new cases in `test/app.test.ts` (a returned `Response` and a thrown `HTTPError`, both in web and node modes). They fail on `main` and pass with this change. The full vitest suite, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` and `tsc --noEmit` pass.

The bundle-size budgets in `test/bench/bundle.test.ts` are raised. The extra branch adds about 150 bytes, and the `defineHandler` budget already failed on `main` (7045 > 7040). New sizes: `H3Core` 8012 B (gzip 3220), `defineHandler` 7204 B (gzip 2942).

Written by an agent (Claude Code, claude-opus-5-5).
